name: K. V. Toys India Limited
sector: Toys: OEM sourcing, final assembly and distribution; emerging controlled manufacturing
research_status: Complete analytical record; identified evidence gaps retained
identity_note: CIN L32409MH2023PLC400074; incorporated 2023-04-04; do not backdate legal issuer to predecessor 2009.
summary: K. V. Toys is primarily an OEM-led toy sourcing, final-assembly and distribution business expanding into controlled manufacturing/creative-product entities. Its strongest demonstrated feature is sales scaling: FY26 economic-continuation revenue grew 38.71%, not the 104.29% issuer-only headline. That is not proof of consumer-brand power. Cash realization remains weak even after correcting the FD classification, new-group incremental returns are unknown, and material historical bank-return discrepancies plus current funding/tradability evidence remain unresolved. At the dated ₹252.45 secondary close, this is a growth-execution research watch, not an established compounder or an actionable value call. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS. Verified lawful cash deployment, productive manufacturing cohorts and repeatable sell-through would change the assessment; category optimism or a lower share price alone would not.
priority: Research priority: current group funding, capital cohorts and exchange execution evidence

quote.status: Dated secondary close; official exchange close not retrieved; not a live executable quote

score_note: NS is missing critical evidence, not zero or a neutral score. GQS cap 5 does not replace NS.

material_facts: Unmodified FY26 audit and disclosed RPTs; IPO is fresh issue, not promoter OFS.
Business transfer, ₹12.4342 crore demand loans, related rent and legacy statutory qualification need stewardship follow-up.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No substantiated severe diversion or minority abuse found; associate explanation and immateriality are preserved.
factor_audit.rationale: Material bank-return and treasury-policy reconciliation weaken stewardship confidence, but disclosure and explanations are preserved and no severe abuse is established. GOV remains 5, not an automatic misconduct penalty; no governance-failure override.

material_facts: 11 OEM partners, proprietary moulds, brands and a distribution network aid sourcing and range.
No primary manufacturing at prospectus Bhiwandi site; no consumer sell-through, premium pricing or stable end-user retention evidence.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Registered marks, SKU range and relationships provide useful distribution assets rather than no differentiation at all.
factor_audit.rationale: Contestable OEM/distribution economics; category growth and trademarks alone do not establish a durable consumer-brand moat.

material_facts: Selected three-year economic sales CAGR FY23–FY26 is 33.21%; five comparable years unavailable.
FY26 underlying continuation growth 38.71% after eliminating FY25 interentity goods flows, versus 104.29% issuer-only headline.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Price/volume split and third-party retail sell-through are unavailable; manufacturing acquisitions complicate future comparisons.
factor_audit.rationale: CAGR ≥30% starts at 9, no trajectory adjustment; limited comparable history and medium confidence ceiling reduce to 8. Four-year CAGR is a disclosed cross-check, not cherry-picked scoring window.

material_facts: General/modern trade and more than 700 claimed SKUs provide multiple distribution paths.
Manufacturing, creative products and small export sales are potential expansion paths, with approvals and new entities.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: High customer/geographic concentration, tiny export base and no established new-factory economics constrain accessible runway.
factor_audit.rationale: Credible domestic distribution runway, but future growth is not automatically accessible at good returns.

material_facts: One-year incremental normalized NOPAT/core-capital diagnostic is 32.38%.
Three/five-year consistent operating perimeter and expensed/capitalized mould, project and subsidiary cohorts are not reconciled.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Reported scale and profit growth are real; lack of attribution is missing evidence, not proof of poor capital returns.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: a one-year transfer-sensitive proxy does not establish durable incremental ROIC versus the reasoned 13–17% capital-cost range; no verified unit-economics substitute.

material_facts: FY26 CFO −₹14.0218 crore; excluding ₹11.5052 crore FD movement leaves −₹2.5166 crore.
FY23–FY24 predecessor cumulative CFO/PAT only 23.31%; FY25 combined operating-CFO diagnostic is also negative.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Much of FY26 reported cash decline is treasury placement, not operating consumption; total inventory barely grew.
factor_audit.rationale: Bank-return reconciliation lowers confidence, without automatically changing the observed poor-cash score. Persistent poor realization across successive periods, not a penalty for the FD classification or one isolated growth year. Apply growth-quality cap of 5 if GQS becomes computable.

material_facts: ₹22.8948 crore cash plus disclosed unutilized IPO assets is meaningful March funding evidence.
₹12.4342 crore interest-free related loans are on demand; new group commitments and allowed deployment constrain liquidity.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Debt fell after IPO and no actual default/recall is reported; cash-only model is deliberately conservative.
factor_audit.rationale: Eligible IPO-FD WC deployment supports the base without rescue. Manageable published base with meaningful linked-stress sensitivity. Current financeability remains unverified rather than asserted failure; missing evidence does not force a distressed score.

material_facts: Continuation revenue grew from ₹73.95 crore FY23 to ₹174.79 crore FY26.
IPO and subsidiary/associate establishment are evidenced, while Q1FY27 manufacturing promise lacks verified utilization and margin delivery.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Own-factory marketing and secondary commencement reports are encouraging but not an audited milestone-to-cash bridge.
factor_audit.rationale: Distribution scaling is demonstrated; expansion execution is mixed/unseasoned, not a repeatable owned-manufacturing record.

material_facts: FY26 owner PAT ₹8.7431 crore is predominantly operating; normalized recurring PAT proxy about ₹8.4020 crore.
IPO increases shares 36.52% but dilutes old ownership 26.75%; current-share EPS ₹13.92 differs from weighted EPS ₹17.11.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Profit growth exceeds cash realization and minority-owned future operations complicate per-share attribution.
factor_audit.rationale: Operating profit progression is positive, but normalized per-share history is short and future consolidation mix unproven. CASH separately captures conversion.

material_facts: Five-year annual EBIT/working-capital/capex models exist at a 15% hurdle.
Current funding not verified, and all cash-only cases breach cash floors including pre-entry.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The segregated eligible IPO-FD WC case supports base cash without rescue, but current allocation and material G2 reconciliation remain unverified.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: material G2 bank-return reliability and current funding are unresolved; ordinary and conditional non-rescue return fields stay null. Separate rescue diagnostics are not R inputs.

material_facts: Bear decline, ten-point working-capital inflation and half-related-loan recall produce large cash deficits.
At the price, 8× bear EBIT and explicit net rescue ₹19.4294 crore leave about 13.63% old-holder dilution and counterfactual negative return.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Promoter interest-free loans and earmarked IPO liquidity are real mitigants; actual default is not established.
factor_audit.rationale: Material permanent-impairment and recapitalization risk under linked stress supports 3, without labeling the business insolvent.

material_facts: P/E on current shares is 18.13×; required-growth sensitivity has explicit 8/12/16× terminal multiples.
No verified funded crossing exists for a reverse-expectations solver.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The eligible IPO-WC base is cash-feasible without rescue, but that does not resolve current balances, bank-return reliability or owner-attributable future earnings.
factor_audit.rationale: NS rather than invent a required CAGR from an infeasible or unverified bracket; P measures price-implied expectations, not business predictability.

material_facts: Current lot 600 and floor reference position 1,800 shares / ₹454,410 are verified by master arithmetic.
Only 49 secondary observed prints; 60-session completeness, zero/no-trade classification, spread and surveillance are absent.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The observed prints show transactions, not a suspension; theoretical capacity is calculated only as a proxy.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: missing histories are not zero-volume days and 49 observed prints cannot earn a canonical 60-day liquidity band.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.rationale: Disclosed related-party financing/transfer and legacy statutory uncertainty warrant scrutiny. No substantiated severe abuse found; clean opinion and associate management explanation retained.
gates.resolution: Clarify predecessor statutory exposure, RPT commercial fairness and new-entity capital allocation.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.rationale: MD&A cash transposition/restatement bridges are resolved, but material Q2 bank-return receivable gaps remain: ₹16.5315 crore in CARO versus ₹17.3840 crore in the notes/prospectus. Stock and Q4 cross-table differences also lack a quantitative reconciliation. Management incomplete-entry/netting explanation, Q3/note-Q4 agreement and clean audit/controls opinions are retained; none resolves magnitude, timing and scope. No fraud finding.
gates.resolution: Auditor-supported quarter-end bridge of gross/net debtor and creditor balances, posted bank entries, submitted security/drawing-power returns and corrections aligning CARO with financial notes.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.rationale: A segregated ₹10.5 crore IPO-FD working-capital-only case funds the base without rescue; eligible deployment does not require assuming unrestricted release. Hold instead reflects unverified current allocation/group uses, callable obligations, drawing-power reliability and linked-stress coverage. The cash-only gap alone is not proof of unfinanceability. No actual default or unavoidable shortfall asserted.
gates.resolution: Recent published IPO utilization/bank-resource note and conservative consolidated sources/uses with call/commitment stress; private daily bank statements are not required.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.rationale: 600-share lot verified, but secondary quote/49-print history and unknown spread/restrictions cannot establish execution of a ₹5 lakh reference position. Absence from NSE daily data is not a no-trade day.
gates.resolution: Complete BSE 60-session turnover/no-trade record, current quote, spread, circuits/surveillance and order-book check.

Its strongest demonstrated feature is sales scaling: FY26 economic-continuation revenue grew 38.71%, not the 104.29% issuer-only headline. That is not proof of consumer-brand power. Cash realization remains weak even after correcting the FD classification, new-group incremental returns are unknown, and material historical bank-return discrepancies plus current funding/tradability evidence remain unresolved. At the dated ₹252.45 secondary close, this is a growth-execution research watch, not an established compounder or an actionable value call. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS. sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Legal issuer: K. V. Toys India Limited; BSE SME code 544641; ISIN INE1IE301018; CIN L32409MH2023PLC400074. The interoperable master label KVTOYS$ is retained exactly, not presented as NSE listing. Information cutoff 20 October 2026; sources retrieved 21 October without using that day’s price. Reference close ₹252.45 on 19 October 2026 is secondary, market cap ₹158.5386 crore on 62.8 lakh shares. Exact five-year equity horizon 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; nominal pretax hurdle 15%, sensitivities 12/18%. Illustrative ₹5 lakh reference rounds down to 3 lots/1,800 shares/₹454,410 or up to 4 lots/2,400 shares/₹605,880, not personalized allocation. Data confidence: high on transcription of signed FY26 statements and lot identity, but low on unresolved bank-return reliability; medium on reconstructed continuation growth and corrected cash presentation; low on current funding allocation, capital cohorts and complete tradability. G1 Conditional; G2/G3/G4 Hold — unresolved.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R NS, D 3, P NS, L NS. Exact BQS known contribution 4.54 at 88% coverage gives raw missing-data bounds 4.66–5.74; GQS known contribution 5.60 at 85% gives 5.75–7.10; IAS known contribution 0.60 at 20% gives 1.40–8.60 because Q must be final BQS, not a midpoint. BQS, GQS and IAS all remain NS. Persistent weak cash conversion triggers only the specified GQS cap of 5 if calculable; capped mathematical bounds coincide at 5 but do not create a score. No governance or evidenced-funding-failure cap applies. All weights, Decimal contributions, confidence and counterfacts are recorded below. A one-point judgment change moves BQS by the factor weight, GQS by its separate weight, and cannot repair missing evidence.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The predecessor KV Impex began in 2009; the listed legal issuer was incorporated in April 2023 and acquired the business in January 2025. Toys include vehicles, guns, dolls, animal/character toys and bubbles. In H1FY26 vehicles were 25.65% of sales, guns 17.03%, dolls 12.93% and animals 12.60%. The prospectus model supplies proprietary moulds/technical requirements to 11 OEM partners, buys semi-finished/finished products and performs final assembly, inspection, packaging and distribution in eight leased Bhiwandi units totaling about 100,000 sq ft. It explicitly denies primary manufacturing at that site. Annual-report claims of 15 OEMs and one owned factory describe a transition, not the historical profit engine. Subsidiary Indo Manufacturers is 55%-owned, Crayonix 65%-owned and Just Bear a 27% associate. FY26 subsidiaries were pre-revenue; future profits cannot all be credited to listed-company shareholders. Cash is collected from wholesale/retail counterparties, with material inventory and supplier advances before final collection.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Proprietary marks Alia & Olivia, Yes Motors, Funny Bubbles and Thunder Strike, mould tooling and channel relationships can help assortment and lead times. Five registered marks and seven pending applications do not demonstrate an enduring premium brand; no material entertainment-license agreement or licensed-sales split was verified, and foreign royalties are nil in FY26 disclosures. Repeat distributor statistics are not household loyalty: the apparent 93.33% FY25 repeat rate follows a denominator collapse during the business transfer. H1FY26 top-five/top-ten concentration of 43.40%/53.82% and Maharashtra above 50% expose local channel risk. Official peers show why the distinction matters: OK Play emphasizes manufacturing and outdoor/preschool products, Funskool a broad owned/partner product portfolio and manufacturing processes, and Mattel globally established franchises. These are business benchmarks, not direct valuation peers. The prospectus’ OK Play FY25 revenue ₹167.7904 crore/PAT loss ₹0.8323 crore is issuer-extracted historical context, not current comparable-market evidence. Durable KV pricing power, consumer pull and channel exclusivity economics remain unproved.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Use three years before scoring because five comparable years are unavailable. FY23 ₹73.9512 crore to FY26 ₹174.7934 crore yields 33.21% CAGR. Original FY22 sales ₹60.2558 crore provide a four-year 30.51% cross-check, not five/ten-year evidence. Annual sales additions are ₹7.6770 crore in FY24, ₹44.3817 crore in FY25 and ₹48.7835 crore in FY26. FY25 issuer ₹85.5601 crore plus ten-month predecessor ₹77.6421 crore less reciprocal sales ₹37.1923 crore equals ₹126.0099 crore; failure to eliminate doubles economic revenue. FY26 grows 38.71% over that denominator. Price versus volume and acquired versus incremental brand demand are not fully disclosed. H1FY26 ₹80.8030 crore and implied H2 ₹93.9904 crore show a 53.77% H2 weight; a management Q3 update around ₹49 crore does not establish long-run seasonality or audited quarterly cash. An October H1FY27 update located through secondary indexing was not retrieved as an underlying filing, so it does not upgrade the trajectory score.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Bottom-up expansion is more distributors/productivity, higher modern-trade penetration, additional SKUs and eventually owned-manufacturing contribution. More than 700 SKUs and 2,000 claimed relationships give access, but the chairman’s 1,400 active wholesalers needs cohort reconciliation. Export ₹0.0348 crore is only 0.020% of FY26 sales, so international expansion is optionality rather than a proven runway. Indo/Crayonix/Just Bear have different ownership and capital requirements; approvals alone do not verify capacity, utilization, contribution margin or cash break-even. A current one-year incremental return proxy is 32.38% versus an assumed 13–17% capital-cost range, but transfer accounting, advances and expensed moulds prevent a valid three/five-year incremental bridge. CAP is NS, not 3. Growth quality is further limited by multiple weak cash years; CASH 3 invokes the formal cap while missing CAP keeps GQS NS. Model expansion cash is explicit scenario spending, not an approved facility or an asserted secondary purchase obligation.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Capital allocation involves the ₹8.9132 crore predecessor acquisition versus ₹8.6038 crore transferred net assets and ₹0.3094 crore goodwill. The ₹8.9 crore earlier business advance, ₹0.0132 crore balance payment and acquired ₹1.8098 crore cash are reconciled, not counted as a new FY25 ₹8.9 crore cash outlay. July 2024 conversion of loans into 45 lakh ₹10 shares is not a bonus issue; the IPO is fresh issuance with no OFS. FY26 director remuneration ₹0.7429 crore is about 8.47% of standalone PAT, alongside disclosed RPT rents/fees and interest-free demand loans. Auditor opinions are unmodified; legacy predecessor PF/ESIC qualification and Just Bear pre-commencement deposits/rent need follow-up, with the company’s recoverability/ratification explanation retained. Delivery record: distribution revenue growth is evidenced; January–February 2026 new-entity approvals and February Q1FY27 production target are evidenced; marketing assertion of one factory is not a verified utilization/returns outcome. The unresolved bank-return discrepancy and IPO mutual-fund placement versus prospectus bank-deposit language warrant clarification, not an automatic misconduct finding. No substantiated integrity failure was established.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Signed FY26 cash flow reconciles opening ₹1.8558 crore + CFO −₹14.0218 crore + investing −₹9.3510 crore + financing ₹25.1529 crore = closing cash equivalents ₹3.6359 crore. MD&A reverses the investing-cash-flow years and calls ₹15.3138 crore cash including FDs; neither supersedes the signed statement. FY25 annual comparative PAT ₹4.5575 crore versus prospectus-restated ₹4.5926 crore differs by ₹0.0351 crore tax/goodwill restatement; CFO −₹18.9504 crore versus −₹19.1868 crore differs by approximately ₹0.2364 crore prepaid IPO-cost presentation. FY26 FD movement ₹11.5052 crore explains most reported negative CFO, but ex-FD CFO remains −₹2.5166 crore and ex-FD free cash after ₹0.5605 crore capex remains −₹3.0771 crore. Receivable days on economically comparable end-balance revenue rise from 47.81 to 50.62; average FY26 receivable days are 42.54. Finished goods increase while WIP falls, supplier advances rise ₹3.9340 crore and payables decline, so unchanged total inventory does not prove a cash-light model. Normalized EBIT removes other income (including the gratuity credit) and prior-period credit once, not legitimate expenses. Owner PAT/current shares gives ₹13.92 EPS, not weighted ₹17.11. A separate material issue remains unresolved: CARO Q2 book debts are ₹24.2428 crore against ₹40.7743 crore bank returns (gap ₹16.5315 crore), while prospectus/annual notes show ₹23.3903 crore against the same bank number (gap ₹17.3840 crore, about 74.3% of book debtors). Q2 stock gap is ₹2.2073 crore in CARO versus ₹2.6904 crore in notes. CARO Q4 stock/debtor gaps ₹0.10/₹0.2166 crore contrast with zero in notes; Q3 agrees in both. Management cites incomplete entries and common debtor/creditor netting, but no numerical quarter-end bridge was obtained. CARO Q2 uses balances matching March year-end, suggesting a possible period/template error, not an established resolution. Clean audit/controls opinions and later agreement are important counterevidence, not proof of Q2 reconciliation. G2 is Hold, without asserting fraud. Historical and annual tables below preserve both versions and separate legal/economic scopes.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Use current-share P/E/PB as checks and a five-year operating-EBIT exit model, not an unsuitable asset-heavy DCF or value for leased operating property. Dated P/E is 18.13×, P/B 2.90×; cash-equivalents-only EV/normalized EBIT after required entry cash is about 14.21×. Annual bear/base/bull growth starts −10%/+20%/+28% with later taper, EBIT margins 4.5–5.0%/6.7–7.0%/7.5–8.5%, terminal multiples 8×/12×/16× and working-capital/reinvestment cash explicitly charged. Future new-entity profitability is not assumed; incremental group-entry cash has no automatic offsetting valuation. Signed terminal cash minus required operating reserves is retained even when negative; no debt plug or extra operating-property value. FY32 cash is included only to 19 October 2031 using its actual 366-day fiscal length. All ordinary IRRs, conditional non-rescue returns and 12/15/18% entry-price fields remain null while funding is unverified; all cash-only scenarios breach a floor. Separate ₹200-per-share, 2%-fee equity rescues show dilution and counterfactual diagnostics, not accessible financing or target prices. A segregated IPO-FD scenario also funds the base with no rescue: use only ₹10.5 crore for existing/incremental eligible working capital, which the prospectus permits, leaving all ₹8.7589 crore mutual funds outside the case. It is not an unrestricted cash assumption or new financing; draws and remaining pool are explicit. Ordinary returns remain NS because material G2 and current allocation/group obligations are unresolved, not because earmarked money is categorically unusable. Reverse expectations stay NS without a verified funded bracket; a search endpoint is not a solved growth requirement.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is a distribution business priced as a scalable brand/manufacturer: channels take longer to pay, fashionable/seasonal inventory turns slowly, supplier advances grow and new factories consume cash before consumer pull is proved. A ten-percentage-point working-capital increase, first-year sales decline, margins at 4.5–5%, 8× terminal EBIT and recall of half the related loans produce a severe negative cash path. Counterfactual net rescue is approximately ₹19.43 crore; new-share expansion 15.78% differs from original-holder dilution 13.63%. The rescue bear price diagnostic is not an ordinary target and still implies a negative five-year return. Actual demand/obsolescence losses can be worse than book-value arithmetic; SKU age, returns and markdowns are absent. Positive counterevidence is substantial earmarked IPO liquidity, declining conventional debt, operating profits and interest-free promoter support. The thesis breaks if growth remains invoice-led without repeat sell-through and cash conversion, or if related support is withdrawn before inventory/receivables monetize.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A fivefold share-price outcome in five years requires 37.97% annual compounding; tenfold requires 58.49%. At current shares, fivefold market capitalization would be about ₹792.69 crore and tenfold ₹1,585.39 crore before further issuance. With an unchanged 18.13× earnings multiple, attributable PAT must roughly reach ₹43.72 crore/₹87.43 crore versus ₹8.74 crore today, and any dilution raises those requirements. At a 7% net margin that implies sales around ₹624.5 crore/₹1,249.0 crore, far beyond simply adding registered marks or announced capacity. The optimistic core model is not verified manufacturing contribution, and no evidence establishes the capital, consumer demand and minority allocation needed for a five/tenfold equity outcome. Treat such outcomes as contingent possibilities, not the base thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor ten specific indicators: (1) FY27 economic revenue and underlying volume/price versus FY26 ₹174.7934 crore, not an issuer-only low base; (2) distributor sell-through, active-customer cohorts and retail returns, currently undisclosed; (3) top-five share versus H1FY26 43.40%, warning above 50%; (4) comparable receivable days versus 50.62, warning above 65 with overdue growth; (5) finished goods ₹17.9703 crore and supplier advances ₹6.8008 crore, warning if they outgrow sales without collections; (6) ex-FD CFO versus −₹2.5166 crore, requiring positive conversion rather than mere FD redemption; (7) object-level IPO deployment and demand-loan balance ₹12.4342 crore, with documented current resources and stress coverage; (8) each subsidiary’s commercial start, external revenue, utilization, invested cash, owner-attributable cash break-even and minority share; (9) official 20/60-session traded value, spread, lot and restrictions before any implementation. (10) obtain an auditor-supported Q2 bank-return reconciliation and align CARO/notes, including gross/net debtors and posted entries; unreconciled ₹16.53–17.38 crore gaps are a reliability hold. These are research milestones, not a promise of ongoing monitoring or trade instructions.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: Hold — unresolved; growth-execution watch with material capital-impairment risk, not an evidenced governance Avoid, insolvency finding or established compounder. No BQS/GQS/IAS point or favorable ranking is assigned while critical factors are NS. Known MOAT 4, CASH 3 and BAL 5 also fail the framework’s compounder requirements independently of missing CAP. The price is relevant but a lower quote does not prove lawful funding or consumer moat. Research priority is the material bank-return reconciliation, then a recent published group cash/obligation bridge, attributable manufacturing capital economics and complete BSE execution evidence. Only then can ordinary return, reverse-price expectations and conditional entry levels be scored. Cash-only deficits are stress diagnostics and the IPO-availability bound is important counterevidence; neither should be misrepresented as today’s exact bank position.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence is the final prospectus, original predecessor accounts, FY26 audited annual report, and dated board/business updates. Competitor official sites are qualitative benchmarks, not independent validation of KV claims; undated live pages retrieved 21 October are used only for established product categories, not post-cutoff events. Market price/history and discovery index are secondary and explicitly limited to dated rows through cutoff. Open questions: quantified Q2 bank-return and CARO-versus-notes reconciliation; IPO mutual-fund interim-placement policy versus prospectus bank-deposit language and management no-deviation statement; primary October half-year/transaction update; current IPO objects/balances and callable financing; manufacturing commercial output and subsidiary profit allocation; end-consumer sell-through and pricing; inventory aging/returns; predecessor statutory exposure; full 60-session BSE turnover and current restrictions. Modeling uses 25% tax, 13–17% capital-cost diagnostic, operating cash at 2.5% sales, no dividends, and explicitly assumed scenario capex/expansion and rescue terms. These assumptions are not management guidance or financing commitments. Source-free analytical copies retain citations, original hashes, numerical extracts and code but not original PDFs/HTML/OCR; reproduction checks arithmetic and consistency, not fresh external authenticity.

evidence.claim: The prospectus claims more than 700 SKUs, 2,000 general-trade relationships and 30 modern-retail chains. FY26 marketing also cites 2,000 wholesalers while the chairman refers to 1,400 active wholesalers. These are not additive independent customers.
evidence.locator: S1 distribution description; S2 opening business review and chairman statement
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: No audited SKU profitability, distributor inventory or retail sell-through series.

evidence.claim: Top five/top ten customers were 43.40%/53.82% of H1FY26 revenue versus issuer-only FY25 19.27%/24.10%. FY25 predecessor concentrations include intra-business transfer and cannot be compared naively. Maharashtra exceeds half of sales in the prospectus risk discussion.
evidence.locator: S1 printed pp.38 and 116 customer concentration
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Many wholesale relationships and multiple channels diversify distribution, but not demonstrably consumer demand.

evidence.claim: Predecessor repeat-customer ratios rose 50.76% FY23 to 66.46% FY24 and 93.33% for ten months to January 2025; the last denominator shrank to 135 customers amid transfer. These are distributor relationships, not consumer retention.
evidence.locator: S1 printed p.137 repeat customers
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: No stable, same-cohort consumer repeat metric exists.

evidence.claim: Comparable economic revenue is ₹73.9512 crore FY23, ₹81.6282 crore FY24, ₹126.0099 crore FY25 and ₹174.7934 crore FY26. FY25 combines predecessor and issuer, eliminating ₹37.1923 crore of reciprocal goods transactions. Three-year CAGR is 33.21%; FY26 growth is 38.71%, not issuer-only 104.29%.
evidence.locator: S1 predecessor/restated history; S2 FY25 RPT purchases ₹34.7444 crore plus sales ₹2.4479 crore; audited revenue note
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Economic-continuation series is not an audited consolidated statement and price/volume split is unavailable.

evidence.claim: Original FY22 predecessor sales were ₹60.255840741 crore; four-year FY22–FY26 sales CAGR is 30.51%. Five- and ten-year comparable series are unavailable.
evidence.locator: S3 original profit and loss; S2 revenue
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Predecessor balance sheet also contains personal/non-operating assets, not assets of the listed business.

evidence.claim: FY26 consolidated owner PAT is ₹8.7431 crore, reported weighted-average EPS ₹17.11 on 5,110,904 shares; current-share equivalent EPS is ₹13.92 on 6,280,000 shares. Fresh IPO issued 1,680,000 shares with no OFS.
evidence.locator: S1 offer structure; S2 consolidated P&L, EPS and capital notes
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: EPS based on weighted shares is lawful but not current fully issued per-share earnings.

evidence.claim: FY26 operating CFO is −₹14.0218 crore. Other-bank balance movement of ₹11.5052 crore largely reflects FDs; an ex-FD diagnostic is still −₹2.5166 crore. FY23–FY24 predecessor cumulative CFO/PAT is 23.31%.
evidence.locator: S2 signed consolidated cash flow; S1 predecessor cash-flow statements
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: FD build is not all operating consumption; do not describe the full reported negative CFO as inventory burn.

evidence.claim: FY26 end receivables ₹24.2428 crore, inventory ₹22.5525 crore, payables ₹13.5967 crore and supplier advances ₹6.8008 crore. FY25 comparatives ₹16.5053/22.1054/14.0190/2.8668 crore. Finished goods rise ₹13.4708 to ₹17.9703 crore despite little total inventory growth.
evidence.locator: S2 consolidated balance sheet and notes on inventory, receivables, other current assets and payables
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Receivables more than six months old are ₹0.8075 crore; inventory aging, returns and markdown loss are not disclosed by SKU.

evidence.claim: March 2026 cash equivalents ₹3.6359 crore, other-bank FDs ₹11.6779 crore and mutual funds ₹8.7589 crore. Unutilized IPO funds total ₹19.2589 crore, comprising ₹10.5 crore FDs and ₹8.7589 crore mutual funds. They cannot be counted twice or assumed freely distributable.
evidence.locator: S2 cash, investments and IPO-utilization notes
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: These assets are substantial positive funding evidence; conservative cash-only scenarios are lower bounds, not claims that earmarked funds are permanently unavailable.

evidence.claim: Gross IPO ₹40.152 crore; equity issue costs ₹3.1954 crore and net equity ₹36.9566 crore. Cash-flow proceeds ₹37.1931 crore differ by ₹0.2365 crore of previously prepaid IPO costs. Offer objects include ₹20.9180 crore working capital, ₹11.6982 crore loan repayment, ₹4.1709 crore GCP and ₹3.3649 crore estimated issue expenses.
evidence.locator: S1 objects; S2 capital, cash flow and IPO note
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Estimated IPO expenses in prospectus differ from actual equity debit; do not subtract both.

evidence.claim: FY26 borrowings total ₹12.5882 crore, including ₹12.4342 crore interest-free related-party loans repayable on demand and ₹0.1540 crore vehicle debt. ₹12 crore sanctioned ICICI line at year-end is not established current undrawn committed liquidity.
evidence.locator: S2 borrowing/related-party notes and credit-line description
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Interest-free promoter support and repayment of IPO-designated debt improve financing; no actual recall or default was identified.

evidence.claim: Indo Manufacturers LLP 55%, Crayonix 65% and Just Bear 27% create new manufacturing/creative-product exposures. March 2026 subsidiaries had nil revenue and aggregate assets only about ₹0.1162 crore; their unaudited accounts were judged immaterial by the group auditor.
evidence.locator: S5/S6/S7 approvals; S2 consolidation and auditor other-matters sections
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Approvals/incorporation are not evidence of commercial plant utilization, unit economics or all future capital needs.

evidence.claim: February 2026 update announced transition from OEM-led model toward own manufacturing and expected Q1FY27 commissioning. Annual-report marketing claims one owned factory. October primary production and expenditure reconciliation was not obtained.
evidence.locator: S4 business update; S2 opening marketing pages
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Secondary reports of May commencement and an October Play Panda transaction are leads, not primary-verified expenditure or economics.

evidence.claim: Auditor gave unmodified FY26 standalone and consolidated opinions. Just Bear emphasis concerns deposits/rent before commencement declaration and management reports recoverable agreements pending ratification. Historical KV Impex PF/ESIC qualification did not quantify possible liability.
evidence.locator: S2 audit reports and associate emphasis; S1 predecessor restated-audit qualification
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Current statutory contribution and an unmodified opinion do not by themselves resolve predecessor exposure; the emphasis is not a finding of diversion.

evidence.claim: FY26 directors remuneration ₹0.7429 crore is about 8.47% of standalone PAT. Related-party loan, rent and professional-fee transactions are disclosed; the business acquisition from predecessor was ₹8.9132 crore versus net assets ₹8.6038 crore, goodwill ₹0.3094 crore.
evidence.locator: S2 RPT note; S1 business-transfer note F-37
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: RPT disclosure supports transparency but does not independently establish arm’s-length fairness or return on allocation.

evidence.claim: MD&A swaps FY25/FY26 investing cash flows and uses closing cash including FDs. Signed FY26 cash flow reconciles ₹1.8558 −14.0218 −9.3510 +25.1529 = ₹3.6359 crore. FY25 restated/annual PAT and CFO differences have identified tax/goodwill/prepaid-IPO bridges.
evidence.locator: S2 MD&A versus signed financial statements; S1 restatement adjustment F-13
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: These errors reduce presentation confidence but are not an unresolved material cash identity once primary statements are prioritized.

evidence.claim: Normalized EBIT proxy ₹12.0989 crore removes other income (including gratuity credit) and prior-period credit once. Current core invested capital ₹42.1972 crore versus prior ₹28.9586 crore gives one-year incremental NOPAT proxy 32.38%, but takeover, supplier advances, expensed moulds and new group perimeter prevent a robust three/five-year attribution.
evidence.locator: S2 P&L, balance sheet and mould/direct-expense notes; model calculation
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: ₹2.2211 crore expensed mould purchases and ₹0.8128 crore capitalized plant/mould balance are not interchangeable; high accounting return is not established project CAP.

evidence.claim: At dated secondary 19 October close ₹252.45, current-share market cap ₹158.5386 crore, current-share P/E 18.13× and P/B 2.90×. Published weighted-EPS P/E would misleadingly compare different share bases.
evidence.locator: M2 OHLCV row; M1 shares; S2 owner profit/equity
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Official BSE closing-price record was not retrieved; price is not live or guaranteed executable.

evidence.claim: Only 49 observed secondary trading prints were obtained. Latest 20-print median close×volume is ₹14.06025 lakh; 49-print median ₹13.1832 lakh. Missing observations are unknown, not zero; spreads and complete 60-session turnover remain absent.
evidence.locator: M2 49 retained observations, August 4 to October 19; M1 lot
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: At the 20-print median, even 10% participation is less than one 600-share lot at reference close.

evidence.claim: OK Play, Funskool and Mattel show differentiated manufacturing/product or brand benchmarks. KV has not demonstrated their manufacturing breadth, catalog IP depth or globally recognized consumer demand. Prospectus peer numbers are issuer-provided and not current market comparables.
evidence.locator: P1/P2/P3 official business pages; S1 peer table p.94
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Peers differ in product mix, country, scale and listing status; none supplies a justified automatic premium multiple.

evidence.claim: FY26 H1 revenue ₹80.8030 crore and implied H2 ₹93.9904 crore mean 53.77% in H2. Q3 management business update reports about ₹49 crore and nine months about ₹129 crore, but no quarter-level sell-through, return provisions or consumer repeat data.
evidence.locator: S1 H1 restated P&L; S4 update; S2 FY26 revenue
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Diverse seasonal/evergreen range can smooth sales, but two halves do not establish a stable seasonal pattern.

evidence.claim: Cash-only base model breaches operating cash before entry by ₹3.1347 crore and needs ₹5.0719 crore net counterfactual rescue to preserve all modeled cash floors. IPO-availability upper bound funds the base but does not establish lawful current allocation or post-acquisition cash.
evidence.locator: Model annual rows and funding sensitivities, derived from S2 balances
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: An unknown balance is not evidence of default. Recent published IPO bank/deployment and group sources/uses can resolve the hold without private daily statements.

evidence.claim: FY26 export revenue ₹0.0348 crore is only about 0.020% of sales. Current sales expansion is primarily domestic OEM/wholesale economics, not demonstrated international brand success.
evidence.locator: S2 foreign-exchange earnings note
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: A nascent German channel provides optionality but no material validated export earnings stream.

evidence.claim: FY26 CARO Q2 book debts show ₹24.2428 crore in books versus ₹40.7743 crore bank returns, gap ₹16.5315 crore. Prospectus F-35 and FY26 notes instead show books ₹23.3903 crore and gap ₹17.3840 crore. Q2 stock gaps also differ: ₹2.2073 crore CARO versus ₹2.6904 crore notes. CARO Q4 has ₹0.10/₹0.2166 crore stock/debt differences while notes show zero.
evidence.locator: S2 printed p90 CARO and pp133/164 notes; S1 F-35
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Management attributes gaps to incomplete entries and debtor/creditor netting. Q3 agrees in both versions, note Q4 agrees, audit and internal-control opinions are unmodified, and no fraud is reported. None quantitatively reconciles Q2 or the inconsistent tables.

evidence.claim: Prospectus working-capital object expressly includes incremental WC and unlocking internal accruals already deployed. A segregated ₹10.5 crore IPO-FD-only scenario funds modeled base eligible WC and cash reserves without rescue; the ₹8.7589 crore MF pool is not used.
evidence.locator: S1 Objects pp81–84; S2 IPO utilization p35; model eligible IPO-WC ledger
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Assumes these March FDs remain available and allocated to WC. Current object breakdown, group cash commitments and bank-return reliability remain unresolved; this is not evidence of an available new facility or present bank balance.

evidence.claim: Prospectus interim-use language describes scheduled commercial-bank deposits, while FY26 discloses ₹8.7589 crore unutilized IPO funds in mutual funds and management states no deviation from objects.
evidence.locator: S1 Interim Use of Funds p88; S2 IPO utilization p35 and directors report p65
evidence.counterevidence_or_limitation: Fund category and relevant permissions/reconciliation were not obtained. Do not infer an equity-market investment, illegality, misuse or fraud from the word mutual funds alone.

bank_return_reconciliation.counterevidence: Unmodified audit and effective-internal-controls opinion; Q3 agrees in both tables; note Q4 agrees and CARO Q4 differences are smaller; no reported fraud/default.

scope_notes: Standalone FY25 and group FY26 are not silently treated as identical; subsidiaries pre-operating in FY26 but future interests not fully owned.
Historical operating lease rent remains in EBIT; no unsupported lease debt or operating-property bonus added.

Future subsidiary capex/ownership profit mix is unverified. Core operating forecasts do not assign incremental manufacturing profits; expansion cash is a conservative non-returning outlay in these scenarios, not a group subscription automatically lost from group cash. Recipient and use are not established, and an internal subscription alone would not be a consolidated cash outflow.
No ordinary return or entry point while funding, material historical bank-return reconciliation and new group perimeter are unresolved; algebraic diagnostic prices are non-investable.
No debt plug. Negative cash is an explicit gap. Earmarked IPO proceeds are not added again to equity value.
Tax assets, payroll/statutory dues, gratuity and ordinary working-capital obligations remain in cash forecast operating assumptions; not double-subtracted at terminal.
